The Silent Drum

The drum hangs silent on the wall,
No hands to make its rhythm call.
Dust settles on its tautened skin,
Where once the spirit danced within.
The dancers' feet are cold and still,
The songbirds left the grassy hill.
A silence heavy, thick, and deep,
Has lulled the village into sleep.
We wait for dawn to break the spell,
And drink from memory's deep well.

content:
The Marketplace

The market was a cacophony of sounds and a riot of colors. Market women shouted their wares at the top of their lungs, competing with the blaring horns of impatience buses. Chike navigated the labyrinth of stalls, holding his wallet tight against his chest. He saw a woman haggling fiercely over a basket of tomatoes, her hands cutting the air for emphasis. The smell of roasted corn battled with the stench of the open gutters. It was chaotic, dirty, and loud, yet it possessed a vibrant pulse that Chike found strangely intoxicating.
